decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach toward the visible coin; keep left at origin. Use small orientation increments and refine coin alignment from wrist view.
Continue right elbow-up arc, advancing toward the holder while rotating the gripper downward. Coin is forward and left of the initial wrist axis.
Advance on a smooth elbow-up arc while pitching the right gripper toward a top-down coin grasp; keep clearance above the holder.
Bring the right wrist above the holder with a downward approach, slowing before finger contact. Final orientation and offset remain visually adjustable.
Complete the downward wrist alignment above the coin with open fingers; inspect centering before closing.
Refine coin centering from the wrist image and lower slightly, bringing the fingers partway closed without yet lifting.
Coin is centered between the right fingers. Close fully at the current pose, then verify retention with a controlled lift.
Lift the closed right gripper vertically away from the holder and check visually that the coin rises with it.
Coin has visibly cleared the holder. Raise it above eight centimeters before the right-to-left handoff; keep the grasp closed.
The coin visibly slipped from the right fingers. Open and hold clear to locate its settled position before attempting recovery.
The coin has settled flat on the right side of the table. Move the open right gripper above it for a low, centered recovery pinch.
Lower cautiously over the flat coin, adjusting sideways from the wrist image and narrowing the fingers while maintaining clearance.
Center the flat coin nearer the fingertip pinch location and lower in small increments to its rim height, keeping the fingers open enough to straddle it.
Use the wrist view to center the coin between the narrowing fingers and descend a few millimeters toward a rim pinch.
Close around the visible coin rim at low height. Confirm the coin remains between the fingers before lifting slowly.
Test the recovery grasp with a short, slow vertical lift while keeping the right gripper closed.
The coin remained on the table during the test lift. Reopen and lower farther to bring the fingertip surfaces to the coin's edge, rather than closing above it.
Adjust the fingertip placement toward the coin rim without forcing farther into the table; narrow gradually for a better edge pinch.
Reposition so the coin edge lies at the distal fingertip pinch point rather than under the wider finger faces; maintain table clearance.
Center the near rim at the fingertip tips and lower only a few millimeters, gradually narrowing around it.
The coin rim is now centered at the tips. Finish closing and perform another small lift to verify retention.
Check whether the coin rim is retained at the fingertip by lifting slowly with the gripper closed; watch for separation.
The coin is not retained. Level the two fingertip heights and reopen over the settled disk for a more symmetric, very low rim grasp.
Use the wrist image to recenter the disk between the level fingertips while descending toward its rim.
Bring the level fingertip edges to the disk rim, using small downward increments and centering from the wrist view. Avoid a large table-directed motion.
Maintain the current low height rather than pressing into the table, follow the coin rim slightly while closing, and test with a minimal lift.
The coin appears centered at both fingertip edges. Lift slowly with the gripper closed and check whether its image stays fixed relative to the fingers.
The coin is visibly moving with the right fingers. Raise it smoothly while maintaining the rim grasp and sufficient clearance for reorientation.
Begin a slow reorientation of the retained coin toward a vertical handoff, moving only within the right workspace. Maintain the closed rim grasp.
Continue turning the retained coin upright and inward; start the left arm's elbow-up approach with open fingers, keeping the arms on their own sides.
Bring the retained disk upright toward the central handoff area while the left open gripper approaches from its own side; keep smooth elbow-up motion.
Continue the separated elbow-up approach to a face-to-face handoff. Keep the right grasp closed and the left fingers open.
Reorient the right-held disk for a perpendicular handoff so the left fingers can pinch its faces rather than its rim. Keep the coin elevated and both arms separated.
Hold the left open gripper short of contact while turning the right-held coin toward a face pinch. Continue slow, separated wrist motion.
Turn the rim-held coin toward a perpendicular left-hand face pinch while keeping it elevated; left remains open and clear until alignment is established.
Finish bringing the upright disk to the central handoff and advance the left open fingers toward its exposed faces without crossing the arm workspaces.
Hold the right-held disk steady and align the left fingertips to the exposed upper portion using the left wrist view. Keep both grippers from overlapping.
The disk slipped during the close handoff approach. Separate and raise both open grippers, then locate the settled coin before recovery.
Clear the central table view and start a downward recovery approach with the right gripper; keep the left withdrawn from the coin and right arm.
The prior approach was rejected without motion. Replan from the unchanged pose with substantially smaller pitch and translation increments.
Move the right wrist laterally clear of the coin to expose its head-camera location, retaining a continuous elbow-up configuration.
The settled coin is near the center. Approach it directly with the left arm from the left side at an angled downward pinch, while withdrawing the right arm clear.
The preceding approach was rejected with zero execution. Halve the left-arm increments to preserve joint continuity; continue separating the right arm.
Continue the left-side angled descent toward the visible central coin, with fingers open. Withdraw the right arm toward its original workspace.
Continue the left angled approach to the coin while keeping the left wrist on its own side; retract the empty right arm toward origin.
Bring the left open fingers toward the coin from the left at a controlled angle, refining the forward offset; continue the right arm's retreat.
Continue the left angled approach, shifting toward the coin center with open fingers; bring the empty right arm close to origin.
Lower the angled left fingertips toward the coin rim while centering laterally. Complete the empty right arm's return to its starting pose.
Center the left fingertips over the disk and lower toward the rim with a gradual partial close, watching for table contact.
Close the left fingers around the centered coin rim with a few millimeters of cautious descent. Keep the right arm parked and inspect retention next.
Test the left rim grasp with a small vertical lift, keeping the gripper closed and watching whether the coin follows.
The coin stayed on the table. Reopen and move the left fingertips slightly farther onto its near rim at low height for a deeper grasp.
Close around the centered rim at the current low height, then make only a tiny lift to check retention.
Test the tilted rim grasp with a slow one-centimeter lift and inspect whether the coin follows the left fingers.
Recenter on the disk after the test lift, level the fingertips, and approach the rim symmetrically with a gradual close.
Correct the lateral alignment toward the visible disk, reopening to avoid pushing it with one finger. Hold low height rather than pressing into the table.
Lift and fully open before correcting alignment, since a low lateral motion pushed the disk. Reposition above its settled center without contact.
Center above the disk while clear, then descend symmetrically with open left fingers to straddle its rim.
Recenter the disk at the distal pinch region, with a brief upward clearance before the lateral correction and controlled descent.
Finish lateral centering and close gently around the low rim. Keep the pose steady to avoid ejecting the disk while the fingers converge.
Reopen and advance the angled left fingertips farther over the disk center, rather than closing on only its near edge. Preserve the left-side wrist position.
Close the left fingers at the current centered position without further table-directed movement; inspect the rim before lifting.
